candidate_claims.text: The 50 bp deletion overlaps the protein-coding gene RNF212 (ENSG00000178222) spanning coordinates 1,056,247 to 1,113,697 on chromosome 4.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: Ensembl baseline annotations establish that the deletion falls entirely within the coordinates of the RNF212 gene.

candidate_claims.text: Ensembl VEP predicts that the 50 bp deletion acts as an intron variant (intron 3/9) with MODIFIER impact on the canonical RNF212 transcript ENST00000433731.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: VEP predicts a modifier impact intronic consequence for the canonical transcript.

candidate_claims.text: Ensembl VEP predicts the deletion acts as an intron variant across multiple alternative RNF212 transcripts, including nonsense-mediated decay and retained-intron biotypes.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: VEP consequence annotations for alternative transcripts indicate intronic localization with MODIFIER impact.

candidate_claims.text: The breakpoint windows of the 50 bp deletion contain Charlie1a repeat elements on both the start and end sides.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: Ensembl baseline repeat annotations and quality control assessment show Charlie1a repeat overlaps at both breakpoint regions, presenting a repeat-region alignment risk.

candidate_claims.text: An active regulatory enhancer ENSR4_8TF7 is located near the deletion coordinates at 1,092,388–1,092,550 on chromosome 4 but does not directly overlap the variant.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: Ensembl regulatory annotations place enhancer ENSR4_8TF7 upstream of the deletion start coordinate.

candidate_claims.text: A partially overlapping candidate deletion (variant ID DEL_chr4_09a860e6) has a reported allele frequency of approximately 57.76% (72,835 alleles observed) in the gnomAD-SV database.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: gnomAD-SV database records a high-frequency 50 bp deletion at chromosome 4 coordinates 1,092,989–1,093,039.

candidate_claims.text: A partially overlapping copy number loss candidate (variant ID gssvL87089) has a reported frequency of 0.462963% (4 out of 864 samples) across multiple studies in the Database of Genomic Variants (DGV) Gold Standard.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: DGV Gold Standard records the gssvL87089 variant overlapping the deletion region.

candidate_claims.text: Multiple identical and partially overlapping structural variant calls, including esv3833873 with 1,914 variant calls, are documented in dbVar.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: dbVar reports multiple coordinate-matched or highly overlapping copy number variants from various submitters and studies.

candidate_claims.text: PubMed search retrieved a study discussing the role of Foxj3 in mouse spermatogenesis (PMID: 27739607), which does not evaluate or mention this specific 50 bp human RNF212 deletion.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: The retrieved paper focuses on FOXJ3 in mouse models and does not establish any link to the investigated RNF212 variant.

candidate_claims.text: Because the deletion is localized entirely within an intron of RNF212 and does not overlap the nearby enhancer ENSR4_8TF7, the transcriptional regulation mediated by this enhancer is inferred to remain unaffected.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: Based on coordinate exclusion of the regulatory element and intronic annotation of the deletion.

candidate_claims.text: Based on the high allele frequency in population databases (57.76% in gnomAD-SV) and VEP-predicted modifier impact, the 50 bp deletion is hypothesized to be a benign polymorphism with no adverse clinical phenotype.
candidate_claims.evidence_basis: Polymorphic frequency combined with intron-only localization suggests a neutral, non-pathogenic variation.

evidence_gaps: No patient-level clinical classifications or phenotypic annotations are available in ClinVar or ClinGen Dosage databases for this specific structural variant.
There is an absence of functional or experimental validation in published literature assessing the expression of RNF212 in carriers of this 50 bp intronic deletion.
limitations: Coordinate overlaps in public databases like dbVar and DGV are based on different mapping pipelines and do not establish identical breakpoints or biological events.
VEP consequence terms are automated predictive models based on transcript models and do not guarantee expression levels or splicing effects in vivo.
PubMed searches are restricted to abstracts and indexing metadata, potentially omitting full-text mentions or supplementary details regarding this variant.

query_provenance.query_summary: RNF212 AND ("structural variant" OR "structural variation" OR "intronic deletion" OR "intron deletion")

identified_evidence_gaps: No patient-level clinical classifications or phenotypic annotations are available in ClinVar or ClinGen Dosage databases for this specific structural variant.
There is an absence of functional or experimental validation in published literature assessing the expression of RNF212 in carriers of this 50 bp intronic deletion.
investigation_log.stop_reason: The candidate is a highly frequent (~58% allele frequency in gnomAD-SV) 50 bp deletion within an intron of RNF212. Whitelisted follow-up actions (such as querying transcripts, exons, or expanding gnomAD retrieval) would not change the interpretation of this common, likely benign population variant.
remaining_limitations: Baseline VEP consequences are predictions and do not rule out potential non-coding regulatory or splicing effects, though such effects are unlikely to be clinically significant given the high population frequency.
Coordinate overlaps in public databases like dbVar and DGV are based on different mapping pipelines and do not establish identical breakpoints or biological events.
VEP consequence terms are automated predictive models based on transcript models and do not guarantee expression levels or splicing effects in vivo.
PubMed searches are restricted to abstracts and indexing metadata, potentially omitting full-text mentions or supplementary details regarding this variant.
